events.summary: Case filed On May 1, 2025, President Donald Trump issued an Executive Order to create the Religious Liberty Commission , an advisory committee focused on “defend[ing] religious liberty for all Americans” and “celebrat[ing] America’s peaceful religious pluralism.” On Feb. 9, 2026, an inter-faith coalition of Plaintiffs, including organizations specifically representing Muslims, Sikhs, and Hindus, filed a complaint against federal officials challenging the composition and disclosure failures of the administration’s Religious Liberty Commission. Plaintiffs argue the Commission as currently constituted violates the Federal Advisory Committees Act (FACA) in two ways. First, Plaintiffs allege the Commission’s members are “almost exclusively” Christian, in violation of FACA’s requirement that advisory committees be “fairly balanced.” Second, Plaintiffs allege the Commission has failed to make available to the public meeting minutes and other Commission records required to be publicly disclosed under FACA. Plaintiffs allege these failures to comply with FACA in turn violate the Administrative Procedure Act’s (APA) mandates that the Administration act lawfully and with reasoned explanation. Plaintiffs seek declaratory and injunctive relief under the APA and the Mandamus Act, declaring Defendant’s administration of the Commission to be arbitrary, capricious, and contrary to the law. Plaintiffs specifically request the Court declare the Commission’s makeup to be unlawfully unbalanced, and enjoin Defendants to both attach a disclaimer noting its unbalanced membership to any reports or recommendations it produces and release to the public documents produced for the Commission.
